narrative: Material PL1__M17AF202 shows erratic daily demand (mean 4,641 units, CV 0.51) with a statistically significant declining trend of approximately 9 units per day. Lead times are moderately unstable (CV 0.47, mean 2.57 days), requiring an effective lead time of 3.28 days for planning purposes. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended: the EOQ-derived order quantity of 30,579 units minimises total replenishment and holding costs, while the safety stock of 11,407 units (z=1.645 at 95% service level) substantially exceeds the current SAP setting of 3,393 units and provides adequate buffer against combined demand and lead-time variability within the 53,952-unit storage constraint.
warnings: Declining demand trend detected (slope=-9.15 units/day, p<0.05); monitor for structural demand shift
Recommended safety stock (11,407) is 236% higher than current SAP safety stock (3,393); review with demand planner before implementation

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand pattern with continuous daily consumption and moderate lead-time variability is best served by a continuous-review fixed-order-quantity model. The (r,Q) policy triggers a replenishment of fixed size Q whenever on-hand inventory falls to reorder point r, balancing ordering frequency against holding costs via the EOQ formula while the safety stock provides service-level protection against the combined stochastic variance of demand and lead time.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding: maximum stock position (safety_stock 11,407 + order_quantity 30,579 = 41,986 units) represents 77.8% of the 53,952-unit storage limit, leaving adequate headroom. No capacity-driven order reduction was required.
